sections.html:
Oklahoma ad valorem taxes come due on November 1. The bill turns delinquent on January 1 unless at least half has been paid by then, and 68 O.S. section 2913 allows no more than two installments.

Payment situationOklahoma rule
Bill dueNovember 1
Whole bill delinquentJanuary 1, unless one half or more was paid before that date
Second halfPayable before April 1, then delinquent
Mortgage servicersOne annual payment before January 1
Bills of $25 or lessFull amount before January 1
Interest on delinquent tax1.5 percent per month or major fraction, stopping once interest equals the unpaid tax

Mailed payments count by the date of receipt, since the county treasurer stamps each envelope with its arrival day. If your lender escrows taxes, you probably never see these dates, because the servicer pays in one lump sum.

sections.h2: Who sets the value of an Oklahoma house for tax purposes?
sections.html:
The county assessor sets the value, and the Oklahoma Tax Commission supplies the rules and forms. Under 68 O.S. section 2875, each assessor must follow the Commission's rules and may not use a form the Commission has not approved.

When the assessor raises a house's fair cash value from the prior year, a written notice goes out by mail, marked with the mailing date. Section 2876 requires it to show the current fair cash value, the taxable fair cash value for the preceding and current year, the assessed value and the assessment percentage for both years, plus the taxpayer bill of rights. For a homestead it must also explain the application for a limit on fair cash value under Article X, Section 8C of the state constitution.

Keep that notice with your sale papers. A buyer's title company will see the same numbers on the tax roll.

The assessor must schedule an informal hearing, which can be held in person or by phone if the taxpayer asks. A taxpayer who cannot attend gets at least two more chances, on alternative dates that fall on different days of the week.

Details in section 2876 that are easy to miss:

  • The protest goes on a form prescribed by the Tax Commission and must set out the facts in plain, concise language.
  • The assessor may fix a scrivener's error or other admitted error at any time, even after the 30-day window closes.
  • The decision comes by regular or electronic mail, marked with the mailing date, and that date starts the appeal clock.
  • If the appeal goes to the county board of equalization, the assessor must give the board the taxpayer's submissions, the data supporting the value, and a written explanation of the informal hearing result.

A protest does not pause the bill. Under section 2884, full taxes must be paid when due during an appeal, and a pending appeal is dismissed if the taxes go delinquent. A taxpayer may also protest an unchanged valuation by the first Monday in April (section 2876(F)).

Every qualifying homestead gets a $1,000 reduction in assessed valuation, and some owners get a second $1,000. The dollar amounts are small, but they come off assessed value, so claim them while you still live in the house.

  • Base exemption: $1,000 of assessed valuation (68 O.S. section 2889).
  • Additional exemption: another $1,000 for heads of household whose gross household income for the prior year did not exceed $30,000 (section 2890).
  • Value limit: a separate application for the Section 8C limit on fair cash value of a homestead (section 2890.1).

Applications go to the county assessor by March 15, or within 30 days of a valuation increase notice if that is later. A late application generally starts with the following tax year, except for certain tornado cases. Owners 65 or older who previously qualified for the additional exemption need not reapply each year, but must tell the assessor if income rises above the limit.

Estates have a duty here too. An executor or administrator must notify the assessor when a homestead is no longer the homestead of an eligible person. Heirs who keep an inherited vacant house should expect the exemption to end. Our homestead exemption guide covers the rules in more detail.

sections.h2: When taxes go unpaid for years
sections.html:
Once taxes have been unpaid three years or more, the county treasurer must advertise and sell the real estate at the county tax resale. Section 3105 sets the resale for the second Monday of June each year.

A county treasurer may run the resale as an online auction, which can start any time during business hours in the full week of the second Monday of June. Property sells to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds, and the cost of an online auction firm is added to each property's sale. Section 3129 also defines "nuisance property" for parcels with liens above fair market value or environmental problems costing more than the property is worth.

An owner, or anyone with a legal or equitable interest, can redeem before the auction starts. Under section 3113, the payer gives the county treasurer the originally delinquent sum, interest at the lawful rate and any accrued costs. Minors and mentally incapacitated owners have one year after the disability ends, with interest and penalty of no more than ten percent a year.

Counties with more than 100,000 people must skip the sale for some owners. The conditions are a single-family home, an owner of 65 or older (or totally disabled) who owes the tax, no rental use, income at or below the federal guideline level, and a tax roll value of $180,000 or less.

Oklahoma imposes a documentary stamp tax on deeds for realty sold, at $0.75 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it. It applies when the consideration exceeds $100, measured without counting liens that remain on the property.

Under 68 O.S. section 3202, several deeds are exempt:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child or close relatives, with no actual consideration.
  • Deeds between a person and that person's own revocable trust.
  • Tax deeds, and deeds of release of property that secures a debt.
  • Foreclosure deeds where the buyer is the mortgage holder.

The tax attaches when the deed is executed and delivered to the buyer. Ask the closing agent to show this line, along with any prorated property tax, on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Selling with back taxes or an open protest
sections.html:
Start by finding out exactly what is owed and which year it belongs to. Call the county treasurer for a payoff figure on delinquent tax; the closing agent then pays it from your sale proceeds.

Section 2885 makes assessor and equalization board proceedings the sole way to correct an assessment or abate taxes, so a value cannot be disputed at closing. When the protest deadline is behind you, the realistic choices are to pay the bill or sell with the valuation as it stands.

Several years of delinquent tax, an inherited house or code violations often block a conventional listing. A cash buyer may purchase such a house as-is, and the title company clears tax liens from proceeds when the numbers allow. Terms depend on the property, and this page is information, not tax or legal advice.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due November 1. If half or more has been paid before January 1, the rest is due before April 1. Otherwise the whole bill is delinquent on January 1.

faqs.q: What interest does Oklahoma charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes bear interest of 1.5 percent per month or major fraction until paid, and interest stops growing once it equals the unpaid principal. A separate five percent monthly penalty applies only to certain nonindividual owners of large property in small-county dependent school districts.

faqs.q: Can I stop a tax sale by paying?
faqs.a: Yes. An owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest may redeem before the resale auction starts by paying the delinquent sum, lawful interest and accrued costs to the county treasurer.

faqs.q: How much is the Oklahoma homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $1,000 of assessed valuation, with another $1,000 for heads of household with prior-year gross household income of $30,000 or less. Apply to the county assessor by March 15.

faqs.q: Is there a deed tax when I sell an Oklahoma house?
faqs.a: Yes. The documentary stamp tax is $0.75 per $500 of consideration when consideration exceeds $100, with exemptions such as certain family transfers without consideration.
